$sources: The photograph frame: the as-built flat oak moulding with softened edges (windows/Source/MuseeVision/Frames/MuseeFrame.cpp, the Photograph style: its face 0.8 of its width above the glass, its sight lip 4 mm, its arrises rounded 3 mm inside and 4 mm outside) and the Hall of Light's sheet (Docs/Stages/hall-of-light.md sec. 3.5: 22 mm fumed oak frames round each mount), re-set as the museum's moulding is (Data/Art/Moulding.json): A outward from the edge of what it frames, B up from the face it rests on (the glazing's, where the work is glazed), in units of the moulding's width, drawn from the outside edge inward.
The width is the sheet's 22 mm whatever the mount's size, as a framer runs one moulding round every print of a series.
The rebate stands 2 mm clear of the mount's edge all round, as the museum's moulding stands clear of a canvas's.

face.source: MuseeFrame.cpp, Photograph: up the outside, round the outer arris, across the flat top, round the inner arris and down the sight edge to the glass.
